title: MDX format inferred from a `.md` path disables the rejection contract entirely
statement: `@mdx-js/mdx` 3.1.1 infers its parsing format from the document path when `format` is not passed. With a `.md` path it parses as plain markdown: JSX is not parsed, so a permitted component renders as a bare paragraph and a JavaScript expression compiles with no error — the rejection plugin sees no nodes to reject and reports success. Passing `format: "mdx"` explicitly restores both the component and the refusal.
notes: ⚠️ THIS IS A SECURITY-RELEVANT DEFAULT, not a formatting quirk. DEC-0020's whole contract is that forbidden JavaScript fails the compile with a diagnostic; under format inference it fails nothing, and the failure mode is silence. Stage documents are `.md` today, so the naive configuration is exactly the vacuous one. ⚠️ THE FIX IS TO PIN THE FORMAT, NOT TO RENAME THE DOCUMENTS. Renaming to `.mdx` would work today and would break again the first time anything reads a `.md` file — the contract would once more depend on a filename rather than on configuration. `format: "mdx"` is passed explicitly in `app/_mdx/compile.js`, and the test fixture is deliberately named `.md` so that dropping the option fails nineteen tests instead of passing quietly.
